# Planetary Moon Count Comparison

This report compares the known number of natural satellites (moons) orbiting Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars, based on current astronomical data.

## Summary of Findings

The gas giants, Jupiter and Saturn, possess significantly more moons than the terrestrial planet Mars. Jupiter holds the record among the three for the highest number of known moons.

| Planet | Moon Count | Comparison |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Jupiter** | 115 | Has the most moons of the three planets. |
| **Saturn** | 146 | Has the highest moon count overall among the three. |
| **Mars** | 2 | Has the fewest moons, consisting of two small satellites. |

***

*Note: Moon counts are dynamic and subject to discovery. The figures used reflect recent astronomical estimates.*

# Planetary Moon Count Comparison

This report compares the known number of natural satellites (moons) orbiting Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars, based on current astronomical data.

## Summary of Findings

The gas giants, Jupiter and Saturn, possess significantly more moons than the terrestrial planet Mars. Jupiter holds the record among the three for the highest number of known moons.

| Planet | Moon Count | Comparison |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Jupiter** | 115 | Has the most moons of the three planets. |
| **Saturn** | 146 | Has the highest moon count overall among the three. |
| **Mars** | 2 | Has the fewest moons, consisting of two small satellites. |

***

*Note: Moon counts are dynamic and subject to discovery. The figures used reflect recent astronomical estimates.*
